holidays.name: National Frozen Yogurt Day
holidays.description: A day to swirl, top and sprinkle your way to a cup of tangy, creamy froyo. Pile on gummy bears, fresh fruit and cookie crumbs, and call it dessert with a halo.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance celebrating frozen yogurt as a lighter cousin of ice cream. Its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Self-serve frozen yogurt shops made it popular to build your own dessert by weight, so a heavy handful of toppings can cost more than the yogurt.

holidays.name: National Chopsticks Day
holidays.description: Pick up your chopsticks and try to eat a whole meal with them, even if you usually reach for a fork. Rice grains, noodles and dumplings are the ultimate test of your skill.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance honoring the utensil used for thousands of years across East Asia. Its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Chopsticks have been used in China for roughly 3,000 years or more, and they spread to Japan, Korea and Vietnam, where each culture developed its own style.

holidays.name: Pay a Compliment Day
holidays.description: A day for handing out kind words, like praising a coworker's great idea, a stranger's fabulous jacket or a friend's terrible-but-endearing jokes. It costs nothing and might make someone's whole week.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin, built around the simple idea that a sincere compliment can brighten someone's day.
holidays.funFact: Studies on kindness suggest that people who give compliments often underestimate how good the compliments make the receiver feel.
